results.name: Walker Ranch Hay Barn
results.description:
Constructed in 1880, The Livestock/Hay Barn complex comprises five interconnected timber- and log-framed structures set on stone, concrete pier, and earthen foundations. The core Hay Storage Barn features a shingle side-gabled roof, vertical rough-sawn siding, mixed windows, and stone/concrete piers, housing an open northern bay and southern stalls. Extending from this volume are three lean-tos: an eastern shed-roof addition with vertical siding and open framing; a center shed-roof addition with horizontal siding and four stalls; and a northeast lean-to with a corrugated gable roof anchored to a north stone retaining wall with a trough. Completing the cluster to the east are the Calf Barn—defined by a dual gable/shed roof, stone foundation, and rough-sawn siding—and a small southern shed-roofed barn with board-on-board siding resting on an earthen floor.

*3D model from photos generated with photogrammetry software 3DF Zephyr v7.531 processing 522 images*

results.name: Modern Coastal Hillside Villa
results.description:
Cliffside Horizon Villa is a modern luxury residence designed on a sloped coastal landscape, combining clean architectural volumes with natural stone elements and expansive glass facades. The villa features a dramatic double-height entrance, panoramic terraces, a spacious outdoor pool area, and seamless indoor-outdoor living spaces.

Built around the harmony of geometry and nature, the design integrates stone retaining walls, elevated pathways, mature landscaping, and carefully positioned viewpoints overlooking the surrounding scenery. Large floor-to-ceiling windows maximize natural light while creating a strong visual connection between the interior and the environment.

This project focuses on contemporary architectural aesthetics, realistic materials, and a balanced composition of stone, glass, concrete, and wood. The result is a sophisticated hillside retreat that blends modern luxury with natural surroundings.

Software: Blender
Category: Architectural Visualization / Residential Architecture

results.name: RESIDENTIAL FLATS 4 FLOORS
results.description:
Designing a four-floor residential building in 3ds Max involves creating a detailed, multi-level structure, often featuring stilt parking on the ground floor with three or four residential floors above (G+3 or G+4). These designs are frequently visualized using V-Ray for realistic rendering of modern exteriors, facades, and balconies. 

Key Design Elements & Workflow in 3ds Max
Structure & Modeling:


Elevation Design: Focus on creating attractive, modern facades, including balcony structures and window frames.
Material Application: Using V-Ray for texturing with materials like modern brick, concrete, and glass for a contemporary look.
Lighting: Utilizing V-Ray lights for realistic daytime (sunlight) and nighttime (artificial) rendering.
